report.summary: Clearing Previous interval and applying silently uses the prior hidden value (15 days).
report.expected: A blank interval should be rejected or visibly corrected before applying, rather than applying a value absent from the form.
report.actual: Clicking Apply closed the picker and applied Previous 15 days, showing October 2026 Count 28.
reproSteps: As an admin, create a People Count metric with Created At by Month, save it and open its detail page.
Open View date range footer, select Previous and enter 15 days.
Clear Interval so the field is visibly empty.
Click Apply.
Observe Previous 15 days filter and October 2026 Count 28 rather than rejection of the blank interval.
report.reason: Works as intended: a blank interval falls back to the last valid value when the filter is applied.

explanation: Failure of an author-created incompatible or invalid configuration is reported as failure of a supported valid workflow. The reviewed errors are recoverable or the invalid draft is blocked at normal activation; allowing configuration or Test to expose that error does not establish a guarantee to prevalidate every combination. This does not excuse corrupting a valid definition or losing unrelated saved data.
verificationGuidance: Repair the invalid value, reference, relation or duplicate name and run a valid positive control.
Read the actual validation or execution error and distinguish invalid-draft testing from the normally activated supported flow.
Establish any promised earlier validation stage rather than inferring it from the ability to edit or save configuration.

report.name: String Title foreign key permits numeric Products ID target, then View details opens a broken question
report.summary: String Title foreign key permits numeric Products ID target, then View details opens a broken question.
report.expected: The model should prevent an incompatible relationship target, or handle traversal without creating an invalid question.
report.actual: Products → ID is selectable and saves on string Title. View details opens Products with filter ID is Rustic Paper Wallet and displays There was a problem with your question.
reproSteps: Create fresh Products notebook model without Summarize and save in Our analytics.
Edit metadata, select string Title column, choose Foreign Key then Products → ID, and Save changes.
Click Rustic Paper Wallet in the Title column, then View details.
report.reason: Works as intended: the foreign-key picker deliberately allows text-to-number targets; mapping product names onto numeric IDs is a misconfiguration that Metabase reports with its standard invalid-input error.

explanation: A visible input transformation is attributed to silent save-time corruption even though the field or preview already shows the effective value before submission. Reviewed controls normalize unsupported characters, dates or precision; saving that displayed accepted value is different from secretly replacing a valid submitted value.
verificationGuidance: Record the input and preview immediately before blur, Apply or Save, then compare the submitted and persisted values.
Check the field-specific normalization contract and a supported-input control.
Do not use this rejection to dismiss hidden value substitution or corruption that first occurs during a completed save.

report.name: Relative date filter silently saves Previous 0 days as Previous 1 day
report.summary: Relative date filter silently saves Previous 0 days as Previous 1 day.
report.expected: Zero should either be rejected with validation or preserved according to explicitly explained semantics; it should not silently become a different entered interval.
report.actual: With Interval showing0, Add filter remained enabled. Saved chip became “Created At is yesterday”; after refresh, reopening showed Interval1 day. The saved metric returned54.22 on the observed average formula rather than retaining the entered zero interval.
reproSteps: Edit an own saved Orders metric definition.
Add Created At filter > Relative date range; keep Previous and days, enter Interval 0.
Add filter and Save changes.
Reload and reopen Edit metric definition and the Created At filter.
report.reason: Works as intended: an interval of 0 previous days is visibly normalized, matching the dashboards relative-date precedent.

explanation: A stale editor is expected to merge another writer's changes or warn about conflicts even though the reviewed contract accepts last-write-wins saves. A full stale-object submission can restore its displayed fields without establishing corruption of the submitted data. This ruling does not cover a promised merge guarantee or loss without a competing write.
verificationGuidance: Check the documented or adjudicated concurrency contract before requiring automatic merging or conflict detection.
Inspect both editors' saved baselines and submitted fields, then repeat without another writer.
Distinguish an accepted stale full-object save from a completed value disappearing without an intervening write.

report.name: Saving a stale metric definition overwrites another user's saved description
report.summary: Saving a stale metric definition overwrites another user's saved description.
report.expected: Changing only the metric definition should preserve another user's independently saved description, or warn about the conflict before discarding it.
report.actual: Maya saved an already-open Average Rating definition (3.47) after Harbor Admin saved description “Primary concurrent metadata edit”. The description reverted to “Maya lifecycle duplicate”, immediately and after refresh. History says Maya modified the query and changed the description. A whole-page AI assertion confirmed no conflict warning or save error.
reproSteps: As Maya, create a fresh shared-collection metric using Count of Sample Database Products (200), with description “Maya lifecycle duplicate”.
Open Edit metric definition and change Count to Average of Rating; run preview (3.47), but leave it unsaved.
In a separate primary Harbor Admin session, edit only the same metric's description to “Primary concurrent metadata edit”; save and refresh to verify that description and Count200 persist.
After the primary save completes, return to Maya's unchanged stale editor and click Save changes.
Open More info, then refresh and inspect description and History: formula is 3.47 but description has reverted to “Maya lifecycle duplicate”.
report.reason: Works as intended for labeling: concurrent edits from a stale editor follow last-write-wins.

explanation: Reading an “Edited” metadata shortcut as a promise to open the revision-history tab directly, when it deliberately opens the information panel on Overview and History remains available separately.
verificationGuidance: Identify the intended destination of that specific shortcut.
Open the separate History tab to verify revisions are accessible before filing a navigation failure.

report.name: Model and metric revision shortcut opens Overview instead of History
report.summary: Model and metric revision shortcut opens Overview instead of History.
report.expected: Clicking the revision-history shortcut should open the History tab so the relevant saved revisions are visible.
report.actual: Clicking the Edited button on a model opened Info with Overview selected and description/fields visible; History was unselected. Independently reproduced on a metric after reload.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval@momentic.ai and open /browse/models.
Click Create a new model, Use the notebook editor, select Sample Database then People, and Save.
Name the model Model QA People and confirm Save.
Open its three-dot menu > Edit metadata, change the ID display name to Person Key, and Save changes.
Click the “Edited … by you” button beneath the model name.
Observe Info opens on Overview; History is a separate unselected tab.
report.reason: Works as intended: the Edited shortcut opens the Info panel on Overview by design (same as dashboards-390).

explanation: Expecting a re-created variable or output column to automatically recover settings deleted when the original entity disappeared. Restoring SQL text with Undo or returning a failed query to similarly named outputs does not necessarily rewind the separate configuration history or restore the old identities. This does not cover metadata lost while the same valid outputs remain present.
verificationGuidance: Inspect whether the intervening operation removed the variable/output and its associated settings.
Distinguish text undo from full-object revision restoration and names from persistent identity.
Test preservation on unchanged valid outputs separately from deletion and recreation.

report.name: Correcting a saved failing SQL model definition clears unchanged column display name and description
report.summary: Correcting a saved failing SQL model definition clears unchanged column display name and description.
report.expected: Correcting the SQL back to the same column names and types preserves saved column display names and descriptions.
report.actual: After saving a missing-column SQL error and correcting it to the original ID/TITLE/AMOUNT schema, the TITLE display name changed from 'Maya SQL Title' to 'TITLE' and its description became empty.
reproSteps: Set TITLE display name to 'Maya SQL Title' and description to 'Title metadata retained across SQL schema edits.' Save and refresh to verify.
Edit the model definition to SELECT missing_qa_column FROM PRODUCTS, run it, and save the failing definition.
Refresh and reopen Edit query definition; replace the SQL with the original two-row schema, changing only the first amount to 14.50. Run and save.
Refresh, open Edit metadata, and inspect TITLE: display name is TITLE and description is empty.
report.reason: Works as intended: a failing query has no result columns, so their metadata is dropped just as when the columns are removed.

explanation: Expecting a field breadcrumb that identifies the physical database column to change with a customized display name. Physical identifiers and display labels serve different purposes, so a correct physical name is not stale merely because the neighboring heading uses the display name.
verificationGuidance: Identify whether the breadcrumb represents the physical column or the editable display name.
Compare renamed and untouched fields with their physical metadata before alleging a missed rename update.

report.name: Field breadcrumb retains the old name after saving a rename
report.summary: Field breadcrumb retains the old name after saving a rename.
report.expected: The breadcrumb identifies the field by its saved display name, QA RELEASE REGION, consistently with the heading.
report.actual: The heading shows QA Release Region and suggested questions use that name, while the final breadcrumb remains REGION.
reproSteps: Open Our data and select Release operations.
Open Tables in Release operations, then Release Requests, then Fields in this table.
Open Region, click Edit, replace the display name with QA Release Region, and click Save.
Compare the saved field heading with the final breadcrumb.
report.reason: Works as intended: the field breadcrumb always shows the physical column name (uppercased by CSS), never the display name, for renamed and untouched fields alike. It still identifies the current field.

explanation: Expecting a model’s Linked tables summary to enumerate every foreign-key target when it describes explicit tables joined by the model query. Foreign-key metadata and actual query joins are different relationships, so an unjoined target’s absence is not a missing-link defect.
verificationGuidance: Inspect the model query’s explicit joins separately from column foreign-key target metadata.
Compare the summary against its intended relationship definition instead of every navigable target.

report.name: Model Info > Relationships 'Linked tables' leaves out tables the model links to through foreign keys
report.summary: Model Info > Relationships 'Linked tables' leaves out tables the model links to through foreign keys.
report.expected: Linked tables should list every table reachable through the model's FK columns. For both 'Orders + People' and a plain Orders model, that is People and Products.
report.actual: 'Orders + People' (id 1) lists only 'People'. 'Orders plain model' (a model whose query is just the Orders table) shows 'This model is not linked to any tables.' The model metadata (GET /api/card/:id/query_metadata) does include the FK targets: USER_ID has fk_target_field_id 4 (People.ID) and PRODUCT_ID has fk_target_field_id 8 (Products.ID), and both People and Products appear in the returned tables.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval@momentic.ai.
Go to /browse/models and open 'Orders + People'. Dismiss the intro modal with 'Start exploring'.
Click the info (i) icon in the header and open the 'Relationships' tab.
Under 'Linked tables', only 'People' is listed. 'Products' is missing, although the model has a Product ID foreign-key column.
Create a model with only the Orders table as its source and no joins (for example New > Model > Orders > Save). In this run it was 'Orders plain model', id 44.
Open the new model, then Info > Relationships. It shows 'This model is not linked to any tables.' even though the User ID and Product ID FK columns point to People and Products.
report.reason: Works as intended: Linked tables lists the tables the model's query joins, not every table its foreign keys point to.

explanation: Calling an explicitly offered, confirmed and undoable type-conversion action a defect because the reporter expects that object type never to support it. Completing the named conversion is not evidence of silent or accidental mutation.
verificationGuidance: Read the action label and confirmation and verify the resulting supported type.
Establish a restriction on that source type before asserting the conversion should not be offered.

report.name: Metric action menu offers "Turn into a model" and converts the metric into a model
report.summary: Metric action menu offers "Turn into a model" and converts the metric into a model.
report.expected: "Turn into a model" should only be offered for saved questions. A metric's menu should offer metric actions only (Edit metric definition, Move, Duplicate, Move to trash, and so on), and a metric should never be silently converted into a model.
report.actual: The metric menu lists: Add to dashboard, Create an alert, Edit metric definition, Turn into a model, Move, Duplicate, Move to trash. Clicking "Turn into a model" and then "Turn this into a model" redirects to /model/44-... . GET /api/card/44 now returns type "model" and display "table". History shows "type changed from :metric to :model", and the page shows the model menu (Edit query definition / Edit metadata / Turn back to saved question).
reproSteps: Sign in as eval@momentic.ai / momentic-eval-1.
Go to /browse/metrics and click the + (Create a new metric) icon.
Pick the table Sample Database → Orders, set the formula to Sum of Total and the default time dimension to Created At, click Save, name it "QA Total Revenue Metric", and save to Our analytics.
On the saved metric page (/metric/<id>), dismiss the "It's okay to play around with metrics" modal and click the "Move, trash, and more…" (…) button.
Observe that "Turn into a model" is listed. Click it, then click "Turn this into a model" in the modal.
Observe the redirect to /model/<id>: the item is now a model (GET /api/card/<id> returns type "model") and it is gone from /browse/metrics.
Cleanup: open More info → History and revert to the previous version.
report.reason: Works as intended: Turn into a model is a deliberate, confirmed and undoable action that is offered for metrics.

explanation: The claimed missing, changed or unusable state is contradicted by a decisive observation or controlled verification of that same claim. Examples include an allegedly lost value remaining intact or an allegedly broken action succeeding under the stated setup. This disproves the checked allegation, not every related workflow or the possibility of a different historical failure.
verificationGuidance: Verify the actual displayed, submitted and persisted values, and the precise action target, instead of repeating the original interpretation.
Repeat the reported setup and a positive control; record what the decisive observation actually establishes.
Keep any different trigger, transient state or accepted neighboring defect separate from the contradicted claim.

report.name: Trash Undo leaves a converted model in the trash
report.summary: Trash Undo leaves a converted model in the trash.
report.expected: Undo restores the model and removes the trash banner.
report.actual: The red 'This model is in the trash' banner remains after Undo.
reproSteps: As Harbor Admin, create a fresh metric from Sample Database > Orders using the default Count formula and save it in the personal collection.
Open its ellipsis menu and choose Turn into a model.
Open the model's ellipsis menu, choose Move to trash and confirm.
While the moved-to-trash notification is visible, click Undo.
Observe the settled page.
report.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review: Undo restores the converted model from the trash.
